title.en: The cell: structure, division and cell theory

text.en: A house is built from bricks. Your body is built from cells, trillions of them, and each cell is alive. From a tiny bacterium to a giant tree, everything living is made of cells.

The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life. Most cells are too small to see, so we study them with microscopes.
The human eye cannot separate two points closer than about 0.1 mm, so most plant and animal cells, which are much smaller, need a microscope.
The cell membrane is made of proteins and lipids. It controls what enters and leaves, and its mosaic-like arrangement of molecules is why it is called the fluid mosaic model.
Cells with no true nucleus are called prokaryotic cells. Their genetic material lies in a region called the nucleoid, while eukaryotic cells have a nucleus.
Plant cells also have a cell wall and plastids. Coloured plastids are called chromoplasts, from the Greek chroma, colour.
Cells grow and divide to replace old, dead or damaged cells. This is how a cut heals and how hair grows back.
Cell division is the process by which new cells are formed from existing cells. The body grows by more cells, not just bigger cells.
Cell theory says all organisms are made of cells (Schleiden, 1838 for plants and Schwann, 1839 for animals), and, as Virchow added in 1855, all cells come from pre-existing cells.

problem.en: Why can a bacterium be called a prokaryote while an onion cell is a eukaryote?

text.en: A bacterium has no true nucleus; its DNA is in the nucleoid.
An onion cell has a nucleus enclosed by a membrane.
So bacteria are prokaryotes and onion cells are eukaryotes.

prompt.en: State the cell theory and one difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all cells have a cell wall

points.en: The cell is the unit of life.
Prokaryotic cells have no true nucleus; eukaryotic cells do.
Cells divide to repair and to grow.
